backend_scripts.name: _preflight-sandbox.sh
backend_scripts.purpose: Sourced helper (not directly executable): greps obj/project.assets.json files for stale /tmp/cursor-sandbox-cache NuGet paths and aborts with 'Run ./scripts/clean-local-build' if found.
backend_scripts.destructive_or_stateful: no - read-only grep over generated build assets; exits 1 on match, mutates nothing
backend_scripts.documented_run_cadence: Never run directly; sourced by add-mig, drop-db, update-db, check-pending-model, create-smoke-dump, wipe-abwab before any EF/db action

backend_scripts.name: access-admin
backend_scripts.purpose: Wrapper that runs the prebuilt QuranDashboard.AccessAdmin tool (dotnet run --no-build) with DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT defaulted to Development; verbs cover identity scan/backfill, permission-catalogue sync, Owner reconciliation, legacy-role inventory/conversion, and authorization preflight.
backend_scripts.destructive_or_stateful: yes - write verbs (identity backfill --apply, catalogue sync, owners reconcile --apply, legacy-roles convert --apply) mutate the configured database; scan/inventory/preflight verbs are read-only. The wrapper itself adds no guard; safety lives in the tool (reasons, --confirm-production)
backend_scripts.docker_db_requirements: PostgreSQL reachable via tool appsettings -> user secrets -> ConnectionStrings__QuranDashboardDb; requires prior qd-build (runs --no-build); no Docker
backend_scripts.documented_run_cadence: Operator/deployment runbook cadence only, not a per-feature gate: staged Phase 2 deployment order, prospective authorization activation, and Phase 10 legacy Admin/Editor cleanup sequence

backend_scripts.name: add-mig
backend_scripts.purpose: dotnet ef migrations add <Name> against Infrastructure with Api as startup project, output to Migrations/.
backend_scripts.destructive_or_stateful: no to the database (generates migration source files only, never applies); stateful to the working tree (writes new .cs/.Designer.cs files)
backend_scripts.docker_db_requirements: .NET SDK; design-time EF tooling; no Docker; preflight for stale sandbox assets
backend_scripts.documented_run_cadence: Only when a migration is explicitly requested (Backend/CLAUDE.md EF Core Migrations: 'Only add migrations when explicitly requested')

backend_scripts.name: check-api-contract
backend_scripts.purpose: API-contract staleness gate: runs export-swagger, then 'npm run generate:api' in the frontend, then 'git diff --exit-code' over openapi/ and src/app/core/api/generated; fails with 'STALE API CONTRACT' if committed output differs. Deliberately excludes the untracked Redoc bundle.
backend_scripts.destructive_or_stateful: no to data; stateful to the working tree (regenerates the committed swagger.json and generated client in place). export-swagger disables the permission-catalogue startup sync so spec generation never mutates a database
backend_scripts.docker_db_requirements: No DB, no Docker; needs .NET SDK (Release build of Api) and npm/node_modules
backend_scripts.documented_run_cadence: After any change that alters what the exporter reads (controllers/DTOs/routes). NOT listed in TESTING_STRATEGY.md at all and not part of any test lane or pre-PR composite - its cadence lives only in READMEs

backend_scripts.name: check-pending-model
backend_scripts.purpose: Wraps 'dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes' for QuranDashboardDbContext with --build (full solution, single-threaded) or --no-build (requires existing Infrastructure+Api output). Never adds or applies a migration.
backend_scripts.destructive_or_stateful: no - read-only model-vs-snapshot check; --build compiles the solution (build artifacts only)
backend_scripts.docker_db_requirements: .NET SDK; no Docker; no live DB needed (design-time snapshot comparison)
backend_scripts.documented_run_cadence: Alongside the 'migration' lane whenever the EF model or schema is in scope (TESTING_STRATEGY.md section 3.5); a separate command, not part of any test lane

backend_scripts.name: clean-local-build
backend_scripts.purpose: Clears all NuGet local caches, deletes every bin/ and obj/ under Backend, restores the solution.
backend_scripts.destructive_or_stateful: yes to build state (wipes the machine-global NuGet cache and all local build output), no to any data; README calls it 'Non-destructive to data'
backend_scripts.docker_db_requirements: .NET SDK; network for restore; no Docker/DB
backend_scripts.documented_run_cadence: On demand when the _preflight-sandbox check reports stale Cursor-sandbox assets blocking EF/db scripts

backend_scripts.name: cleanup-test-runtime
backend_scripts.purpose: Removes Docker containers/networks of exactly one test-backend run: selected by all five project test labels AND an exact 32-hex run ID. Never prunes, never touches unlabelled resources or dev volumes; reports the Testcontainers reaper but leaves it running; --dry-run lists only.
backend_scripts.destructive_or_stateful: yes but tightly scoped - docker rm --force --volumes, restricted to project-labelled resources of the named run ID; a container already removed by its test host counts as cleaned
backend_scripts.documented_run_cadence: Called automatically by test-backend's EXIT trap on every run; run by hand only to clear a killed run

backend_scripts.name: create-smoke-dump
backend_scripts.purpose: Regenerates the canonical quran_* data-only pg_dump + manifest at resources/db-dumps/quran-canonical/ that the backend Smoke data tier restores. Guards: requires --yes; refuses non-local hosts without --allow-remote; refuses migration-count drift vs the tree; refuses drift in five pinned baseline row counts; atomic temp-file rename of dump and manifest together.
backend_scripts.destructive_or_stateful: yes to the local artifact (overwrites the ~1/3 GB dump and manifest outright); read-only against the source database (pg_dump only)
backend_scripts.docker_db_requirements: Local PostgreSQL with the canonical data; psql + pg_dump >= 18 matching the server; connection from ConnectionStrings__QuranDashboardDb env or API user secrets; no Docker
backend_scripts.documented_run_cadence: After a reseed, and 'Any migration invalidates the dump. Regenerate it ... in the same change' - i.e. every EF migration forces a regeneration

backend_scripts.name: drop-db
backend_scripts.purpose: dotnet ef database drop --force against the configured connection.
backend_scripts.destructive_or_stateful: YES - DESTRUCTIVE: drops the whole configured database, all data lost. Fails closed unless the single argument is exactly --yes; no remote/local distinction - acts on whatever dotnet ef resolves
backend_scripts.docker_db_requirements: PostgreSQL (whatever the configured connection points at); .NET SDK; no Docker
backend_scripts.documented_run_cadence: Local-dev only, on demand; README warns it must never be pointed at the Railway production DB

backend_scripts.name: export-swagger
backend_scripts.purpose: dotnet tool restore + Release build of the Api project + Swashbuckle CLI 'swagger tofile' writing Frontend/quran-dashboard-ui/openapi/swagger.json. Runs from the build output dir; sets Access__PermissionCatalogueStartupSync__Enabled=false so generating a spec never mutates a database.
backend_scripts.destructive_or_stateful: no to any DB (startup sync explicitly disabled); stateful to the tree (rewrites the committed swagger.json); always performs a Release build
backend_scripts.docker_db_requirements: .NET SDK only; no running server, no DB, no Docker
backend_scripts.documented_run_cadence: On demand / as the first step of check-api-contract; no standalone cadence documented

backend_scripts.name: qd-api
backend_scripts.purpose: Runs the API with the https launch profile, --no-build, and polls /api/health to auto-open Swagger.
backend_scripts.destructive_or_stateful: mostly no - dev-server launcher; the running app can write to the configured local DB (it is the live API), so stateful at one remove
backend_scripts.docker_db_requirements: PostgreSQL with seeded quran_dashboard DB, user secrets connection, trusted dev cert, prior qd-build; no Docker

backend_scripts.name: qd-build
backend_scripts.documented_run_cadence: After backend code changes, before qd-api/access-admin

backend_scripts.name: qd-ui
backend_scripts.purpose: Starts the Angular dev server over HTTPS (npm run start:https) after checking node_modules and mkcert localhost PEMs exist.

backend_scripts.name: reset-db
backend_scripts.purpose: drop-db --yes followed by update-db: an empty database at migration head.
backend_scripts.destructive_or_stateful: YES - DESTRUCTIVE: full drop + recreate; --yes gated; discards canonical quran_* data (must be re-imported) and authored abwab curation data (unrecoverable)
backend_scripts.documented_run_cadence: Step 1 of the 'Rebuilding the local database from nothing' runbook; local-dev only, never against Railway

backend_scripts.name: test-backend
backend_scripts.purpose: The single supported Backend test runner. Lanes (summary only; test detail is another agent's scope): fast, access, access-db, migration, process, smoke, tier-b, canonical-data, feature (FEATURE_KEY | --class | --test), pipeline [--feature], pre-pr. Selection is resolved from the class catalog test-gates.tsv (header-verified); it prints lane, selected rows, expanded filter, and resource needs as the evidence block. --build compiles the solution once single-threaded; --no-build verifies the outputs the selection needs (test dll always, AccessAdmin for Migration/Process, DataImporter for Pipeline/Canonical). Any lane selecting SmokeDataReadTests alongside other classes runs as two sequential shards (shared postgres:16-alpine, then exclusive postgres:18-alpine) with a bounded wait for zero project containers between them. Canonical selections preflight required resources and fail (not skip) when missing, printing 'canonical data tier: ran|failed|not selected|discovery only|failed preflight'. Each run exports a 32-hex run ID and an EXIT trap calls cleanup-test-runtime for it.
backend_scripts.destructive_or_stateful: yes at runtime - starts Docker PostgreSQL containers (postgres:16-alpine shared runtime, postgres:18-alpine exclusive for the smoke data class) and removes its own labelled resources on exit; never touches the dev database
backend_scripts.docker_db_requirements: Docker for any non-Fast selection; canonical lanes additionally require staged resources/import-sources/ and the quran-canonical dump+manifest; must not run concurrently with another Backend test process (cross-process OS lock)
backend_scripts.documented_run_cadence: Governed entirely by TESTING_STRATEGY.md sections 3 and 5 (the README deliberately does not repeat selection policy): focused lanes during implementation, tier-b at milestones/review/ordinary pre-PR, pipeline/canonical only on their triggers, pre-pr once for shared-infra/release/full-regression

backend_scripts.name: update-db
backend_scripts.purpose: dotnet ef database update - applies all pending migrations to the configured database.
backend_scripts.destructive_or_stateful: yes - schema-mutating against whatever connection is configured; NO --yes gate (unlike drop-db/reset-db); README warns never to point it at the Railway production DB
backend_scripts.documented_run_cadence: Backend/CLAUDE.md: 'Do not run dotnet ef database update unless explicitly requested'; used inside reset-db and the rebuild runbook

backend_scripts.name: wipe-abwab
backend_scripts.purpose: TRUNCATE ... RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE over a literal six-table abwab_* allowlist, for schema changes that cannot survive existing abwab rows. Post-wipe tripwire: quran_surahs must still hold 114 rows.
backend_scripts.destructive_or_stateful: YES - DESTRUCTIVE: permanently empties authored curation data that nothing restores; --yes gated; localhost/127.0.0.1 only with deliberately NO remote override; CASCADE is safe only because the FK closure of the six tables is internal to the list
backend_scripts.docker_db_requirements: Local PostgreSQL + psql; connection from ConnectionStrings__QuranDashboardDb env or API user secrets; no Docker
backend_scripts.documented_run_cadence: On demand, as the sanctioned local reset when a migration cannot survive existing abwab rows (e.g. 20260802062011_RequireAbwabDoorSection); preferred over reset-db when only abwab rows must go

redundancy_flags.detail: The matrix schedules focused lanes during implementation, then tier-b (+smoke/access as scoped) again at milestone, AGAIN at engineering review, AGAIN at pre-PR. TESTING_STRATEGY.md:250-252 explicitly deduplicates review and pre-PR evidence ('the same final-state run when the tree and environment have not changed'), but the freshness rule (TESTING_STRATEGY.md:48-51: evidence produced before the most recent change is stale) means ANY post-review fix - even a one-line finding fix - invalidates the whole boundary evidence and forces the broad lanes to rerun. Repetition is designed-in whenever review produces changes, which is the common case.

redundancy_flags.flag: Backend pre-pr lane always rebuilds, discarding fresh build state
redundancy_flags.detail: Executing pre-pr 'always builds once' and rejects --no-build (test-backend:144-152), so a pre-pr run immediately after a tier-b --no-build run against the identical tree performs a full single-threaded solution rebuild (-m:1, BuildInParallel=false) that adds nothing. check-pending-model --build and export-swagger likewise each run their own full/Release build on every invocation regardless of freshness.

redundancy_flags.flag: test:pre-pr compiles overlapping TypeScript three times
redundancy_flags.detail: The composite runs typecheck (two tsc projects over app+spec sources), then build:verify (ng build - full AOT compile), then test:full (the test builder compiles its own bundle again, as TESTING_STRATEGY.md:289-290 itself notes). Three compilations of largely the same surface in one sequential gate, plus the two parity checks re-run even when the access catalogue is untouched.

redundancy_flags.flag: Every migration drags the canonical smoke dump and canonical tier in, regardless of scope
redundancy_flags.detail: 'Any migration invalidates the dump. Regenerate it with Backend/scripts/create-smoke-dump --yes in the same change' (TESTING_STRATEGY.md:186-188) - so an access-schema or abwab migration with zero Quran-data impact still forces a dump regeneration (pg_dump of a ~1/3 GB artifact plus baseline verification), and SmokeDumpGate makes stale dumps fail loud in any canonical-bearing lane afterwards. Backend pre-pr always includes the canonical shard, so full-regression on any scope runs importer-backed canonical classes.

redundancy_flags.flag: Backend contract tweak cascades into the full Frontend composite
redundancy_flags.detail: The Backend-only exemption (TESTING_STRATEGY.md:223-228) is void the moment check-api-contract regenerates the committed client: the regenerated files under Frontend/ count as Frontend changes, which per the same rule triggers the focused contract/authorization lane, typecheck, and then test:pre-pr. A one-line response-shape change on the backend therefore buys the entire 5-leg frontend composite.

It appears in no lane, no pre-PR composite, and nowhere in TESTING_STRATEGY.md (grep-verified absent); its only cadence anchor is a README sentence ('run it after any change that alters what the exporter reads' - Controllers/README.md:169-170), and the same README records that the committed spec once stayed stale for several commits precisely because nothing scheduled the check. Defensive/repeated manual runs each cost a full Release build + npm codegen.

redundancy_flags.flag: Review workflow front-loads a large instruction-reading budget
redundancy_flags.detail: engineering-review must always read CODING_PRINCIPLES.md + TESTING_STRATEGY.md (33.4KB); conditionally 3 backend architecture docs, 4 frontend architecture docs + PRODUCT/DESIGN, the test-guard SKILL (12.5KB) + up to 3 references (20KB) when tests are in the diff, and for Spec-Kit changes additionally SPEC_KIT_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW.md (8.7KB) + spec.md/plan.md/tasks.md/contracts/quickstart. The clean-code-guard pack (56.8KB, ~14.2k tokens) is consultable per-finding. A cross-stack Spec-Kit phase review can prescribe on the order of 100KB+ (~25k+ tokens) of documents before the diff is read, and re-review after fixes re-prescribes the same set.

redundancy_flags.flag: deploy-smoke overlaps the build gates at the same pre-PR boundary
redundancy_flags.detail: deploy-smoke triggers 'before a final review / before opening a PR' and verifies restore+build+boot - repeating the dotnet build / ng build work that the test lanes (--build), build:verify, and test:pre-pr already perform at the same boundary. Its unique value (runtime boot + migration-target inspection) is bundled with redundant build verification.

redundancy_flags.flag: commit-workflow invites a third round of the same checks at commit time
redundancy_flags.detail: 'Run relevant Backend/Frontend checks for changed areas when feasible' before committing (commit-workflow/SKILL.md:117) is unscoped: on a boundary where review evidence and pre-PR evidence already exist, an agent following it literally re-runs lanes a third time per commit.

redundancy_flags.flag: speckit-implement's generic template pushes per-phase verification that TESTING_STRATEGY forbids
redundancy_flags.detail: The upstream speckit-implement template mandates 'Validation checkpoints: Verify each phase completion before proceeding' and completion-time 'Validate that tests pass and coverage meets requirements' (speckit-implement:157,177), while TESTING_STRATEGY.md:341-343 orders the phase orchestrator to NOT run broad lanes automatically for every phase. Read literally, the two documents give conflicting cadence; the strategy claims authority (TESTING_STRATEGY.md:11-15) but the tension invites repeated broad runs.

It names no lanes itself; lane selection defers to TESTING_STRATEGY.md via the workspace instruction files.

Root CLAUDE.md:57-58 sequences it: planning-artifact deletion commit only after this review passes.
